outcome: Mode of delivery (cesarean section, vaginal delivery, instrumental and assisted breech delivery)
Neonatal outcomes (low birth weight, low APGAR score at five minutes, required neonatal resuscitation, required NICU hospitalization, neonatal mortality)
cohort: One hundred pregnant women identified with uterine fibroids via USG findings were enrolled in the study.
finding: Pregnancies complicated by uterine fibroids are frequently associated with a high rate of cesarean sections and adverse neonatal outcomes, classifying them as high-risk pregnancies.
mod_finding: The most common mode of delivery was cesarean section (62%), followed by vaginal delivery (25%), indicating a high rate of C-sections in pregnant patients with uterine fibroids.
